title: Common pose-trajectory CSV
description: The single interchange format all three tracking pipelines are normalised to. One row per frame for which the pipeline reported a pose. This is the contract between the extraction stage (which runs under different interpreters, and in one case inside a container) and the evaluation package: extraction writes it, evaluation validates it on load, so a change in an extractor surfaces as a load-time error rather than as a silently different number.

x-format.header: required, exactly the columns below, in this order

columns.description: Column order is significant; readers may address by name but writers must emit this order.

items.name: Frame
items.description: Zero-based index of the row within this file. Note this is NOT a reliable frame identifier for the cuVSLAM pipelines: cuVSLAM renumbers its output sequentially, so an input frame it dropped leaves no gap here. Omitted frames must be counted from Timestamp, as round(dt / median(dt)) - 1.

items.name: Timestamp
items.description: Acquisition-platform clock, inherited from the recording. Integer milliseconds since the Unix epoch. This is the authoritative time base for the whole analysis.

items.name: Translation_X
items.description: Camera position in the SLAM world frame W, which is initialised at the camera pose when tracking begins.

items.name: Rotation_X
items.description: Camera orientation as a ROTATION VECTOR (axis-angle), not Euler angles. Read with scipy Rotation.from_rotvec. Misreading these three columns as Euler angles produces an orientation-dependent gain error of up to 20 percent on every rotational metric, which is a defect this project has actually suffered.

items.name: Pose_Confidence
items.description: ZED SDK pose confidence, 0-100. Empty for the cuVSLAM pipelines, which report no equivalent.

items.name: Tracking_State
items.description: ZED SDK positional-tracking state. Empty for the cuVSLAM pipelines.

items.name: Spatial_Memory
items.description: ZED SDK spatial-memory state (INITIALIZING, SEARCHING, OK, MAP_UPDATE, KNOWN_MAP, ...). The cuVSLAM pipelines write the literal string 'cuVSLAM' here as a provenance marker; this is how a reader tells the two families apart from the data alone.

items.name: Odometry
items.description: ZED SDK odometry status. Empty for the cuVSLAM pipelines.

items.name: Tracking_Fusion
items.description: ZED SDK fusion mode (VISUAL, INERTIAL, ...). Empty for the cuVSLAM pipelines.

x-frames.world: SLAM world frame W, initialised independently per recording at the camera pose when tracking begins.

camera_by_pipeline.zed-sdk: left optical sensor, in the ZED SDK right-handed Y-up convention
camera_by_pipeline.zed-cuvslam: the configured base frame (base_link), ROS convention
camera_by_pipeline.rs-cuvslam: the configured base frame (camera_link), ROS convention

x-frames.note: These differ by constant rigid transformations, which the robot-world/hand-eye calibration absorbs. They therefore do not affect the reported residuals.

x-known-variations.line_endings: Three of the four rs-cuvslam files as originally produced used CRLF while the fourth used LF; pandas tolerates both, so no published number was affected. The release normalises all files to LF.
x-known-variations.number_formatting: The pivot-repeat trajectories were regenerated later and write integral values as '0' where the others write '0.0'. Numerically identical.
